leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members state optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as their round-1 preferred configuration. All five name the same two laureates and the same core credit: Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstration, Ye for taking the strontium clock to the 10^-18 level. All five also record the same reservation, that the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems narrow the novelty margin. They differ on how much the unreached redefinition of the second and the omitted contributors (Takamoto, Lemonde, Ludlow, Derevianko) should count. Johansson and Olsson moved to this position after the opening round, and Pearce moved from IceCube. Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce each name B038 or B033 or B043 as alternatives, so the support is a first preference, not a settled consensus. Three further members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig) list B002 as an alternative and not as their preferred part.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as a single-part prize. They share the argument that a quantitative theoretical prediction (2011) was followed by an experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity (2018) that has been reproduced widely and opened moire quantum materials. They also share the same stated weaknesses, an unresolved pairing mechanism in a field of about eight years and experimental credit (Cao and others) that falls outside the three names. Their citations differ in emphasis: Eriksson words it around prediction and discovery of correlated states, while Mehlig adds that the citation should avoid claiming an explanation of superconductivity. Six members list B038 as an alternative, so it has the widest second-choice support, though Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each judge it less mature than B002.

One member prefers the experimental Higgs discovery (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee), arguing that it is mature, independently confirmed and not covered by the 2013 theory prize. Danielsson himself identifies attribution as the decisive weakness, since three founding-era leaders stand in for two collaborations of thousands, and lists B002 and B038 as the better-attributed alternatives. Several colleagues (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) accept the scientific case but say they cannot support it unless a principled credit rule is found. Nobody else lists B053 in a preferred configuration or as an alternative in round 1.

areas_of_agreement: All eight preferred configurations are single-part prizes; none proposes a shared prize of two or more separate achievements, although Eriksson says in a response that he could accept B002 as the second part of a two-part prize.

Every member who addresses B002 accepts the underlying science: the magic-wavelength concept, accuracy near 10^-18 and independent reproduction in several national laboratories. The dispute is about novelty, timing and credit, not about whether the result is real.
The names Katori and Ye for B002, and the trio MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer for B038, are used identically by every member who proposes them.
Members across several subfields accept that the Higgs discovery is scientifically exceptional and mature, and the objection to B053 is attribution under the three-person limit.

Several members (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Mehlig, Eriksson) treat the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits as a reason for caution about a circuit QED prize; circuit QED (B017) appears in no member's round-1 preferred configuration and in only one alternatives list (Johansson).
The citation for B002 should be built around the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice and its realisation, not around precision metrology in general (stated by Kroll, Johansson and Olsson).
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks are a new discovery or invention, or an excellent refinement of a line already honoured by the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes (Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce raise this against their own preference; Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig weigh it more heavily).

Whether the conceptual and discovery content of moire flat bands and correlated states exceeds the quantitative metrological advance of the clocks (Mehlig and Eriksson argue yes; Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Olsson argue that a settled result should come first).

Whether the Higgs discovery, as an answer to a specific long-standing question of the Standard Model, outweighs the clocks on scientific weight (Danielsson) or whether its collaborative character makes it unsuitable for this prize configuration (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce).

Whether the IceCube diffuse flux, which Pearce lists as an alternative, supports a citation by itself or depends on source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) that remain statistically modest (Lindroth, Johansson, Danielsson).
attribution_disputes: B002: whether a two-name credit (Katori, Ye) is fair given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and the theory of Derevianko, and how to divide credit between the lattice concept and the long JILA programme.

B038: whether the experimental credit can be limited to Jarillo-Herrero when Cao and other early authors did much of the bench work, and whether earlier twisted-bilayer theory and moire experiments (for example Dean, Kim) are fairly omitted.

B053: whether Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee, as founding-era leaders, are the fairest three names, or whether discovery-year spokespersons or analysis leaders should be credited instead (Danielsson raises this himself, Lindroth and Pearce echo it).
B017 (cited in discussion, not preferred): four credited names for three seats, with Blais, proposer of the 2004 scheme, the contested omission (Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Lindroth).

B033 (listed as alternative by Kroll and Lindroth): the experimental credit is split among several ion-trap laboratories, including Wineland and Monroe at NIST, so the three-name allocation is contestable (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce).
maturity_disputes: B038: whether a field of about eight years with an unresolved superconducting mechanism is mature enough. Eriksson and Mehlig regard the flat-band and correlated-insulator phenomenology as robust and independently reproduced; Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Danielsson and Pearce would wait.

B002: whether the redefinition of the second should be awaited or whether demonstrated 10^-18 performance and independent confirmation are already sufficient (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Johansson all note this as open, none treats it as decisive).
B043: whether the IceCube result is a finished discovery (the 2013 diffuse flux) or a discovery in progress, since the origin of most of the flux is unknown (Pearce, Johansson, Lindroth, Danielsson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll-Stefan disclosed a possible perceived connection to B002 through a documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, with Jun Ye associated with Hall's group and JILA. He does not call it decisive and asks whether he should abstain on B002; Danielsson and Johansson treat it as a perceived link to be recorded.

Johansson-Goran disclosed that he directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works on circuit QED at Chalmers, with Chalmers colleagues in superconducting circuits, so his advocacy on B017 may be discounted or he may recuse; he states no conflict for B002 or B038.

Olsson-Eva disclosed that she works in the electron microscopy community with Chalmers colleagues and would recuse on B055 (aberration correction), and noted that Johansson is also at Chalmers for circuit QED discussions.
Pearce-Mark (chair) disclosed that IceCube (B043) is scientifically close to his astroparticle work; he lists it as an alternative and records no tie to the credited names for B002, B043 or B038.

Danielsson-Ulf noted that his black hole research is thematically adjacent to the Event Horizon Telescope (B051), with no documented link to the credited names; Eriksson noted that his field is close to B038 and B015 with no documented link to the credited people; Mehlig noted that KPZ touches topics adjacent to his research. None is a documented conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B002, can the committee state in one sentence what the citation recognises that the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes did not, using the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice and its realisation as the stated basis?

For B002, is a Katori-Ye allocation defensible against the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Derevianko, and should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second or treat 10^-18 performance as sufficient?

For B038, can the pairing mechanism be left explicitly outside the citation, and is the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero alone fair given Cao and the other early authors? Eriksson and Mehlig should say what evidence would make the field mature enough, and the five members who rank it as an alternative should say what would raise it above B002.

For B053, is there a principled rule (founding leadership, discovery-year spokespersons, or analysis leadership) that would let three names carry a discovery made by two collaborations? Danielsson should say whether he would keep it first without such a rule, and the others should say whether any rule would change their ranking.

Should Kroll abstain or be recorded as perceived-connected on B002, given that his is one of five stated first preferences, and does the committee want Johansson and Olsson's recusal statements applied to B017 and B055 in later stages?

Does any member want to propose a two-part prize? If so, which pair (for example B002 with B038, which Eriksson said he could accept), and which attribution and maturity trade-offs would that resolve or create?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows five explicit first preferences for B002, two for B038 and one for B053, with B038 the most frequent alternative and no member preferring B017, B043, B033, B015 or B056. The B002 support is wide in specialty but rests on a single case, that attribution and maturity are clean, while every supporter also records the same novelty and credit reservations. B038 is argued mainly on conceptual novelty and rejected mainly on maturity, and B053 on scientific weight and rejected on attribution. Several statements changed after reading the opening round, so the support counts above are positions explicit in the eight files and not predictions of the final ballot.
